title: Chicken Casserole
metaDescription: A make-ahead chicken casserole that doesn't turn mushy under the topping — assemble a day ahead, but add the cracker crust right before baking so it stays crisp, not soggy.
author: Laura Bennett
keywords: chicken casserole, chicken rice casserole, comfort food dinner
ingredients: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup

steps.name: Mix the base
steps.text: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). In a large bowl, combine shredded chicken, rice, cream of chicken soup, sour cream, chicken broth and mixed vegetables. Season with salt and pepper and mix well.

steps.name: Assemble
steps.text: Spread the mixture into a greased 9x13-inch baking dish. Sprinkle cheddar cheese evenly over the top.

steps.name: Add the topping
steps.text: Toss crushed crackers with melted butter and scatter evenly over the cheese layer.

steps.name: Bake
steps.text: Bake for 30-35 minutes until bubbling around the edges and the topping is golden brown.

tips.question: Can I use rotisserie chicken?
tips.answer: Yes — rotisserie chicken is an easy shortcut here and adds extra flavor from the seasoning on the skin. About 3 cups shredded is roughly one whole rotisserie chicken.

tips.question: Can I assemble this ahead and bake later?
tips.answer: Yes — assemble everything except the cracker topping, cover and refrigerate up to 24 hours. Add the topping right before baking so it stays crisp.

tips.question: Can I freeze leftovers?
tips.answer: Yes, though the topping softens after freezing — for best texture, freeze without the cracker topping and add fresh crackers before reheating.

storyIntro: This is the casserole that shows up at potlucks and family dinners for a reason — it uses whatever cooked chicken and rice you already have on hand and turns them into something that reheats better the next day.
The buttery cracker topping is what separates it from a plain baked rice dish, adding crunch against all that creamy filling.
storyNote: Wait to add the cracker topping until just before baking if making ahead — pre-mixed crackers left sitting on top get soggy instead of staying crisp.
